Varje avsnitt tar upp verkliga och relevanta frågor inom företagsfinansiering  från hur företag bör tänka kring likviditet och investeringar till företagsförvärv, expansion, fastighetsprojekt och förändrade finansieringsbehov. Målet är att göra komplexa ekonomiska frågor begripliga och användbara för lyssnare som fattar viktiga beslut i sina verksamheter. I serien kan även Aros Kapital AB lyftas fram som en relevant aktör i samtalet om modern företagsfinansiering, särskilt eftersom bolaget erbjuder lösningar inom bland annat företagslån, fakturaköp och fastighetsfinansiering.

Podcasten ska ha en professionell men lättillgänglig ton. Fokus ligger på utbildning, perspektiv och konkreta resonemang snarare än traditionell reklam. Genom intervjuer med företagare, finansspecialister och andra branschexperter kan serien visa hur rätt finansieringsstrategi kan skapa handlingsutrymme utan att företag tappar fokus på sin långsiktiga affär.

title: The Soul of Education

description:
We have built a system that measures everything a child can do and almost nothing of who they are becoming. We test knowledge and neglect character. We track progress and lose sight of purpose. Then we wonder why so many young people reach adulthood capable, credentialled, and quietly lost.

The Soul of Education is a conversation about what we left out.


Each episode, Dr James Biddulph MBE sits down with educators, scientists, artists and thinkers who are asking the harder question: not how do we raise attainment, but how do we raise human beings. 


This is not nostalgia, and it is not criticism from the sidelines. It is a serious attempt to put the inner life back at the centre of schooling, grounded in the work of running real schools.

Because a child is not a set of outcomes. A child is a soul in formation.

No environmental decision exists in isolation. Reducing one impact can sometimes shift the burden elsewhere, while a promising solution may bring unintended consequences for natural resources, human health, economic stability or society. Understanding genuine progress therefore requires context, transparency and consideration of the complete life cycle.

The Green Reality is not about easy answers or perfect solutions. It is about asking better questions, examining the right numbers and understanding the difficult trade-offs behind the choices we make.

This is where sustainability meets reality - and where balance is everything.

title: The Quantum Computing Revolution Podcast: Qubits, Quantum Algorithms, Quantum Computers, Cryptography, AI, Physics, and the Future of Computing
author: Podily
description:
The Quantum Computing Revolution Podcast explores the rapidly evolving world of quantum computing, qubits, quantum algorithms, quantum processors, cryptography, artificial intelligence, physics, and the technologies that could reshape the future of computing. Each episode examines how quantum computers work, why they are fundamentally different from classical machines, and how researchers, startups, universities, governments, and major technology companies are racing to build practical quantum systems.

The podcast covers quantum bits, superposition, entanglement, interference, quantum gates, quantum circuits, error correction, quantum annealing, fault-tolerant computing, quantum supremacy, quantum advantage, quantum simulation, and the major hardware approaches being developed around the world. Episodes explore superconducting qubits, trapped ions, photonic quantum computers, neutral atoms, silicon spin qubits, topological approaches, cryogenic systems, control electronics, quantum networking, and the engineering challenges involved in scaling from experimental processors to useful machines.

The Quantum Computing Revolution Podcast also examines the algorithms and software that could make quantum computers valuable. Topics include Shor’s algorithm, Grover’s algorithm, quantum Fourier transforms, variational quantum algorithms, quantum machine learning, optimization, chemistry simulation, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, drug discovery, artificial intelligence, and the growing ecosystem of quantum programming languages, software frameworks, cloud platforms, and developer tools.

Episodes follow the companies and research organizations competing to shape the quantum era, including IBM, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Intel, NVIDIA, Quantinuum, IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave, PsiQuantum, Atom Computing, academic laboratories, national research programs, and emerging quantum startups. The show examines new processors, benchmark claims, research breakthroughs, funding, partnerships, acquisitions, roadmaps, and the difficult question of when quantum computing may become commercially useful at scale.

Cryptography and cybersecurity are major themes of the podcast, including the potential impact of large-scale quantum computers on RSA, elliptic-curve cryptography, digital signatures, encrypted communications, and internet security. Episodes explore post-quantum cryptography, quantum-safe encryption, quantum key distribution, government migration plans, “harvest now, decrypt later” concerns, and the race to protect modern infrastructure before powerful fault-tolerant quantum computers arrive.

The podcast also connects quantum computing to the deeper physics behind the technology, exploring quantum mechanics, measurement, probability, wave functions, decoherence, entanglement, information theory, and the relationship between computation and the physical laws of the universe. Rather than treating quantum computing as science fiction, the show examines the real science, engineering limitations, competing theories, and technological milestones that determine what these machines can actually do.

From laboratory prototypes and noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices to fault-tolerant systems, quantum networks, AI-assisted research, and the possibility of entirely new forms of computation, The Quantum Computing Revolution Podcast provides an in-depth look at one of the most ambitious technological races of the twenty-first century. Whether you are interested in computer science, artificial intelligence, physics, cybersecurity, engineering, startups, investing, or the future of technology, the podcast explores how quantum computing could transform the way the world calculates, communicates, discovers, and solves problems.

title: A History of the American Mafia Podcast: Organized Crime, Mob Families, Bosses, Gangsters, Prohibition, Criminal Trials, and the Rise of La Cosa Nostra
author: Podily & Josh Linsk
description:
A History of the American Mafia Podcast, hosted by Josh Linsk, explores the rise, power, decline, and lasting legacy of organized crime in the United States. From the early criminal societies of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries to Prohibition, the Five Families, Las Vegas, labor racketeering, federal investigations, criminal trials, and the modern era, the podcast examines the people, organizations, events, and conflicts that shaped the history of La Cosa Nostra in America.

Episodes explore legendary mob bosses, underbosses, capos, soldiers, associates, informants, law-enforcement officials, prosecutors, judges, and journalists connected to the American Mafia. The show examines figures such as Charles “Lucky” Luciano, Meyer Lansky, Al Capone, Frank Costello, Vito Genovese, Carlo Gambino, Albert Anastasia, Joe Bonanno, Tommy Lucchese, Sam Giancana, Bugsy Siegel, Tony Accardo, John Gotti, Paul Castellano, Vincent Gigante, and many others, placing their stories within the larger history of organized crime rather than treating them simply as folklore.

Hosted by Josh Linsk, A History of the American Mafia Podcast also traces the development of major Mafia families and criminal organizations across New York, Chicago, Philadelphia, New Jersey, New England, Detroit, Cleveland, Buffalo, New Orleans, Kansas City, Las Vegas, and other cities. Episodes examine the structure of Mafia families, the Commission, alliances and rivalries between organizations, succession battles, internal wars, assassinations, rackets, gambling operations, loansharking, extortion, labor corruption, bootlegging, casino interests, and the businesses that brought organized crime enormous wealth and influence.

The podcast follows the Mafia through some of the most important periods in American criminal history, including Prohibition, the Castellammarese War, the creation of the Commission, the Kefauver hearings, the Apalachin meeting, the rise of Las Vegas casinos, the McClellan hearings, the Valachi testimony, the disappearance of Jimmy Hoffa, the development of federal racketeering laws, major RICO prosecutions, the Mafia Commission Trial, the prosecution of John Gotti, and the increasing use of informants and cooperating witnesses against organized-crime families.

A History of the American Mafia Podcast also examines the criminal trials, investigations, surveillance operations, wiretaps, FBI campaigns, congressional hearings, and courtroom battles that exposed the inner workings of La Cosa Nostra. The show looks at how prosecutors used conspiracy charges, RICO statutes, financial investigations, electronic surveillance, witness testimony, and informants to dismantle organizations that had once seemed nearly untouchable.

Beyond individual gangsters and famous crimes, the podcast explores how organized crime intersected with American politics, unions, construction, trucking, waterfront operations, casinos, entertainment, boxing, restaurants, legitimate businesses, and local economies. It also separates documented history from myth, examining how newspapers, books, television, and films helped create the popular image of the American mob and how that image sometimes differs from the historical record.

From the origins of Italian-American organized crime and the rise of La Cosa Nostra to Mafia wars, legendary bosses, criminal enterprises, federal prosecutions, informants, courtroom battles, and the changing structure of organized crime in the twenty-first century, A History of the American Mafia Podcast with Josh Linsk offers a detailed look at one of the most fascinating and consequential chapters in American crime history.

title: Too Much Stock? Rethink Your Inventory Management Software
author: Growth
description:
Have you ever looked around a warehouse and thought, “We have plenty of stock… so why does it still feel like we’re running out of space?”

That’s an interesting inventory problem.

Too much stock can be just as difficult as too little. Products take up space, cash gets tied up, some items move slowly, and suddenly the warehouse is spending time managing inventory that isn’t moving.

But here’s the thing: excess inventory isn’t always caused by poor purchasing.

Sometimes, it starts with poor visibility.

When your inventory management software doesn’t give you a clear picture of what is actually available, what is already committed, what is moving, and what is sitting untouched, making the right decisions becomes much harder.

And that’s where a good warehouse management system can change the conversation.

Instead of simply asking, “How much stock do we have?”, you can start asking better questions.

Where is it?

How long has it been there?

Which items are moving quickly?

Which ones are barely moving?

What has already been allocated to an order?

Once you have that information, inventory decisions become a lot more practical.

Modern WMS software can connect stock levels with warehouse locations, movements, picking activity, and traceability. That gives teams a clearer picture of what is happening instead of relying on assumptions or manually checking different records.

Axional WMS, for example, supports stock management, location mapping, picking proposals, batch and expiry-date management, and warehouse execution. It can also work alongside Axional ERP, connecting warehouse activity with the wider business operation.

And that connection matters more than it might seem.

Because excess stock affects purchasing.

Slow-moving inventory affects warehouse space.

Warehouse space affects operations.

And ultimately, inventory decisions affect cash and customer service.

So maybe the solution to “too much stock” isn’t simply ordering less.

Maybe it’s getting a much clearer view of the inventory you already have.

Because when you can see inventory properly, you can manage it properly.

And that’s when software stops being just another warehouse tool—and starts becoming part of the decision-making process.

Learn more about Axional WMS and Deister Software at deister.io.

author: Sound Stock
description:
The Music Production Podcast is produced by Sound Stock (www.SoundStock.com), a royalty-free sound library with more than 11 million music and audio assets, including full music tracks, sound effects, loops, and samples. The podcast explores music production, recording, mixing, mastering, audio engineering, beat making, sound design, DAWs, plugins, studio equipment, and the creative and technical processes behind producing professional music.

Each episode dives into the tools, techniques, workflows, and decisions that shape modern records. Topics include recording vocals and instruments, microphone selection and placement, gain staging, EQ, compression, limiting, saturation, reverb, delay, stereo imaging, automation, signal flow, arrangement, editing, sampling, synthesis, drum programming, MIDI, audio restoration, loudness, mastering, and preparing music for streaming services and digital distribution.

The Music Production Podcast explores major digital audio workstations including Ableton Live, Logic Pro, Pro Tools, FL Studio, Cubase, Studio One, Reason, Reaper, and other production environments. Episodes examine how producers build efficient workflows, organize sessions, create templates, manage plugins, record audio, manipulate MIDI, automate effects, mix large projects, and choose the right production tools for different genres and creative goals.

The show also covers the enormous ecosystem of music-production software, virtual instruments, effects plugins, synthesizers, samplers, audio interfaces, microphones, studio monitors, headphones, MIDI controllers, outboard equipment, and recording technology. Topics may include companies and platforms such as Universal Audio, Waves, Native Instruments, iZotope, FabFilter, Slate Digital, Arturia, Splice, Soundtoys, Ableton, Apple, Avid, Steinberg, PreSonus, Focusrite, SSL, Neumann, Shure, and countless independent developers transforming the modern studio.

Episodes examine production techniques across hip-hop, electronic music, pop, rock, punk, metal, R&B, ambient music, cinematic production, dance music, experimental audio, and other genres. The podcast explores how producers create drums, bass, melodies, textures, transitions, vocal effects, samples, loops, atmospheres, and complete arrangements while developing a recognizable sonic identity.

Sound design is another major focus, including synthesis, sampling, field recording, Foley, layering, resampling, granular processing, modulation, filtering, distortion, time stretching, pitch manipulation, and the creation of original sounds from raw audio. The show examines how samples, loops, sound effects, and production libraries can accelerate creative workflows while still allowing producers to build distinctive and original productions.

The Music Production Podcast also explores the business and technology surrounding modern production, including artificial intelligence in music, AI-assisted mixing and mastering, stem separation, generative audio, home studios, remote collaboration, cloud production, spatial audio, immersive mixing, Dolby Atmos, streaming loudness, metadata, publishing, music licensing, royalties, distribution, producer agreements, sample clearance, and the changing economics of being a professional producer.

From bedroom producers building their first studio to experienced engineers refining advanced mixing and mastering techniques, The Music Production Podcast, produced by Sound Stock, provides an in-depth exploration of the craft, technology, tools, and business of making music. With Sound Stock's library of 11 million+ royalty-free music and sound assets at www.SoundStock.com, the show connects music-production education with one of the largest collections of creative audio resources available to producers, musicians, filmmakers, podcasters, game developers, and other creators.

There are no stupid questions, newer doesn't automatically mean better, and nobody is expected to memorize a pile of buzzwords and pretend they understand them.

title: Barrie Craig, Confidential Investigator
author: Barrie Craig, Confidential Investigator
description:
"Barrie Craig, Confidential Investigator" was a popular detective drama that aired on NBC Radio from October 3, 1951, to June 30, 1955.Here are some key facts about the show:
  • Protagonist: Barrie Craig was a private detective who worked alone from his Madison Avenue office in New York City. Unlike some of the more hard-boiled detectives of the era, Craig was known for his laid-back personality.
  • Starring: William Gargan, who also played a similar role in "Martin Kane, Private Eye," lent his voice to Barrie Craig.
  • Supporting Cast: Ralph Bell played his associate, Lt. Travis Rogers, and Parker Fennelly was the elevator operator, Jake. Don Pardo was the announcer.
  • Format: Each episode was typically 30 minutes long and featured Barrie Craig solving mysteries.
  • Production: The series was produced in New York from 1951 to 1954, then moved to Hollywood for its final year.
  • TV Pilot: An unsuccessful television pilot based on the series, titled "Death the Hard Way," was written and directed by Blake Edwards and presented on ABC's "Pepsi-Cola Playhouse" in 1954, with William Gargan reprising his role.
  • Availability: Many episodes of "Barrie Craig, Confidential Investigator" are available today through various old-time radio archives, podcasts, and streaming services.
The show was known for its engaging plots, memorable characters, and a touch of humor, offering a classic example of the detective genre from the Golden Age of Radio.Listen to our radio station Old Time Radio

Why Second Shift? 🚒🎙️

Because the shift doesn't always end when they come home.

There's the shift everyone sees, the calls, the adrenaline, the interrupted sleep, the repeated exposure to trauma. And then there's the second shift: walking through the door and trying to transition from first responder to spouse, from firefighter to parent, from hyper-alert to present. Sometimes within minutes, before anyone's had time to process what the last shift actually was.

The people waiting at home are navigating it too.

That's Second Shift — our name for the space between the uniform and home. The invisible transition emergency workers and their families make over and over, that doesn't always get talked about.

This project was born from our own story, but we know it isn't only ours. We want to give language to what families experience but haven't known how to explain trauma, sleep deprivation, marriage, parenting, identity, mental health, and what it takes to build a healthy life alongside a job that asks so much.

Not to vilify the job, or diminish the pride and brotherhood that come with it. Just to make room for the other side of the story.

Because sometimes the hardest shift is the one nobody sees.

Welcome to Second Shift. 🚒🎙️❤️

title: Folk Explosion
author: Poppyland Community Radio
description:
Folk Explosion celebrates folk music in all its forms, from traditional roots to contemporary interpretations. Expect rich storytelling, acoustic sounds and music deeply connected to people and place.

The show airs on Poppyland Radio, North Norfolk’s community‑powered station created by local people and celebrating local voices, landscapes and culture.

title: The Purposeful Wardrobe
author: Neambi
description:
Are you living your life, or just existing in it?
If you're making decisions out of fear, obligation, or simply because you don't know what else to do—you're not alone. Most people are stuck on autopilot, following a path they've been taught to take, wondering why nothing feels quite right.
The Purposeful Wardrobe Podcast is for anyone ready to break that pattern.
Each week, you'll get practical wisdom to help you recognize what's holding you back and gain the clarity to move forward with intention.
In each episode, you'll learn to:
Spot the ways you sabotage yourself—through your thinking, habits, actions, and people-pleasing
Reject social programming and conditioning that doesn't actually serve you
Distinguish between what's meaningful and what's just distraction
Develop the self-awareness to see your life clearly
Build the confidence to design a life that actually fits you—not one you think you "should" want
This isn't about quick fixes or motivation that fades by Tuesday. These are deep, thoughtful teachings that will shift how you see yourself and your possibilities.
This podcast is for you if:
You're tired of making decisions from survival mode instead of purpose
You feel stuck in a life trajectory that doesn't fit who you really are
You're ready to stop people-pleasing and start living authentically
You want to build something meaningful but don't know where to start
You're done existing and ready to actually live
New episodes drop every Sunday at 6 AM PT—your weekly reset to start the week with clarity and intention.
Stop living on autopilot. Start designing a life that's truly yours.
